title: Fitting the Practice, Not the Works: A Human-Referential Theory of AGI（拟合实践，而非作品：AGI 人本拟合论）
description:
This repository contains the manuscript, codebook, coded corpus, and reproducible analysis for a theory of artificial general intelligence in three connected claims. Conceptually, AGI is a philosophical concept: as long as "generality" is referenced to the open set of human practice, it cannot be reduced to a technical specification. In implementation, the means of AGI is the fitting of human practice — not the fitting of humanity's accumulated works; the theory's core is a temporal clause: "The object of fitting is not humanity's works but its practice — the full spectrum and the full course of human experience. The stock has a wall; the flow does not." Normatively, AGI should be positioned as an augmentative tool, not a new subject.

To make the theory auditable, we built a structured evidence map: a purposefully sampled corpus of N = 80 works coded on two stance axes (descriptive and normative) and eight fitting-object dimensions with explicit/implicit modality. Key quantified results: the experience-type coverage axis (success/failure, expert/novice, typical/marginal) is explicitly treated in 0/80 works (exact binomial 95% CI [0.0%, 4.5%]) while implicitly touched in 9/80; practice-as-flow is explicit in only 2/80 works, both from 2026; a registered absence-search (8 query families across arXiv, ACL Anthology, and Chinese-language web search) confirms zero D8-explicit hits. Four termination boundaries for flow-side fitting and explicit falsification conditions are stated.

This paper builds on a prior empirical audit of failure data in LLM training (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23355929); engineering protocols for practice-flow data are future work. Includes the English manuscript (LaTeX + PDF), the codebook (dual stance axes A1/A2 + dimensions D1–D8 + modality rules R1–R5, CR1–CR6), the full coded corpus (80 works × 24 fields), and a single-file reproduction script.

v1.2.0 (2026-10-19): post-freeze literature re-check incorporated. Engages AI-feedback parity results (RLAIF, Meta-Rewarding, RLSVR, pluralistic-preference curation) via a restated open-domain claim (corrective signal as non-self-grounding); restates the wall as a novelty wall against corpus self-play and synthetic expansion; extends the D8 demarcation against adjacent 2026 coverage work (cultural-signal coverage = D6, trajectory-type diversity, RL prompt-set diversity) with the 0/80 result surviving a logged 2026-10-19 re-check; downgrades METR to a fallible proxy; adds quantified collapse anchors, fitting-lag measurements, and contamination measurements for B4. 28 verified references added (79 to 107). The evidence-map corpus (N=80) and all empirical numbers are unchanged.

v1.2.1 (2026-10-20): Chinese-edition line edit under a consolidated translationese rubric. Fixes a factual gloss error (leximin mistranslated as 最小最大化/maximin; corrected to 词典式最小化), a broken clause in the subjectivity-boundary passage, the systematic mid-sentence "vs" residue (8 sites), coined compounds glossed or reworded (出处分层 now defined at first use; 毒性清洗/单元行/类型性 reworded), internal coding-jargon leaks (CR2/T3 glossed), and translationese in the v1.2.0 insertions. English edition unchanged from v1.2.0.
